extra.message: Unauthenticated POST /create extracts a URL from req.body.content and concatenates it into child_process.exec('identify ' + url). The regex permits shell metacharacters, allowing attackers to append arbitrary commands executed with the application's privileges.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command

extra.message: POST /login passes req.body.password directly into a MongoDB query without requiring a string. Supplying a known email and password: {"$gt":""} matches the user's nonempty password without knowing it. Any matching result grants an authenticated administrative session.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: Authenticated POST /account_details passes the entire request body as rendering options. Validation leaves additional properties intact, so layout: '../package.json' selects a file outside views and returns its contents. Other readable text files can also be selected. Layout resolution is confirmed in the [hbs implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pillarjs/hbs/v4.0.4/lib/hbs.js).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: GET /login forwards req.query.redirectPage to this unescaped EJS expression inside an HTML attribute. A value containing "><script>alert(1)</script> breaks out of the input element and executes JavaScript in the application's origin.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: After successful login, req.body.redirectPage reaches res.redirect without destination validation. The login form also propagates this value from the query string, allowing a crafted login link to redirect users to an attacker-controlled website.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: GET /users is mounted without authentication and always retrieves account ID 1, independently of the caller. It returns the complete record, including name, address, and role, to anonymous clients.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: POST /users permits anonymous callers to persist user records and accepts req.body.role without an authorization check or role restriction. Attackers can create arbitrary records marked as admin. No downstream use of that role is required to exploit this unauthorized database modification.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: Startup automatically creates admin@snyk.io with the fixed password SuperSecretPassword when the account is absent. This runs without an environment restriction or required password change, giving anyone who knows the source credentials access to administrative routes on a fresh installation.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: User passwords are stored as plaintext strings. The administrator seed writes the literal password at line 52, and routes/index.js:39 authenticates by comparing the submitted password directly against this field. Database disclosure therefore exposes usable passwords immediately.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: Startup logs the complete MongoDB URI, including credentials when provided through service bindings or environment variables. It also logs the fetched administrator documents, which contain plaintext passwords. Anyone with access to application logs can recover these credentials.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The application authenticates to MySQL as root using the hardcoded password root. docker-compose.yml configures the same root password and publishes port 3306. These shared demo credentials provide database access wherever the corresponding root account is reachable.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The live chat authentication table contains the fixed credentials user/pwd. findUser accepts this shared password for PUT /chat, allowing anyone who knows the source to impersonate the chat user and submit messages.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The chat administrator password is generated with Math.random(), a noncryptographic random generator. This value protects the canDelete privilege, so the authentication secret lacks the unpredictability required of a security credential.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: The session middleware uses the public, fixed signing secret 'keyboard cat'. Anyone who knows this key can generate valid session-cookie signatures, undermining cookie integrity. This does not by itself create authenticated server-side session state.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: The authenticated session cookie is configured without secure: true, allowing browsers to transmit it over HTTP and expose it to network interception. The [express-session defaults](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/expressjs/session/v1.17.2/README.md) confirm secure is false unless configured.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The server exposes the login and authenticated routes through plain HTTP. The supplied Docker configuration publishes this listener directly on port 3001. When accessed through that deployment path, passwords and session cookies traverse the network without transport encryption.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: Successful authentication sets loggedIn on the existing session without regenerating its identifier. An attacker who can plant a known valid session cookie in a victim's browser can reuse that identifier after the victim logs in and inherit the authenticated session.

cwe: CWE-384: Session Fixation

extra.message: POST /login accepts browser form submissions without a CSRF token or Origin/Referer validation. A malicious site can submit attacker-selected valid credentials through a cross-origin form, causing the victim's browser to establish an authenticated session for that account.

cwe: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery

extra.message: The public login handler performs password checks without rate limiting, backoff, or account lockout. No preceding middleware limits authentication attempts, allowing repeated online password guessing against known email addresses.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: Global multipart upload middleware runs before authentication with no file-size or file-count limits. Uploads are buffered in memory, and /import consumes importFile.data. Anonymous clients can exhaust process memory with large uploads. Buffering and configurable limits are documented in the [upload middleware documentation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/richardgirges/express-fileupload/master/README.md).

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: Unauthenticated POST /import synchronously extracts every entry of an uploaded ZIP without limiting expanded size, entry count, or compression ratio. A highly compressed archive can consume excessive CPU, memory, and disk space while blocking request processing. This issue does not require an archive-library vulnerability.

cwe: CWE-409: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data

extra.message: Each authenticated PUT /chat permanently appends attacker-controlled data to a process-global array without a retention limit or quota. The publicly hardcoded user/pwd credentials permit repeated submissions that exhaust memory; GET /chat additionally serializes the entire growing array.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: Unauthenticated POST /update/:id dereferences todo in an asynchronous database callback without checking err or whether the document exists. A syntactically valid nonexistent ObjectId returns null and triggers an uncaught TypeError outside Express's synchronous error handling, terminating the process.

cwe: CWE-248: Uncaught Exception

extra.message: Development mode enables errorhandler responses containing exception details and stack traces. The supplied startup and Docker configuration do not set NODE_ENV=production, leaving this enabled by default. Malformed input, such as a non-string login username, can trigger responses revealing server paths and implementation details.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The MongoDB service publishes port 27017 on all host interfaces without configuring authentication. Clients able to reach that port can read or modify application collections directly, including the plaintext administrator password, independently of application authentication.
